reason: The cited evidence shows ML potentials can reach near-DFT accuracy for energies/forces in multicomponent alloys (E1) and that ANNs can predict formation energies with <5% error (E3), but none of the passages address free-energy surfaces, vibrational/anharmonic entropy, thermodynamic integration speedups, or fusion property accuracy. The key premises therefore lack specific prior support.
premises: ML potentials can achieve near-DFT accuracy for elemental and multicomponent systems
Sparse training on high-fidelity ab initio data is sufficient to capture free-energy surfaces
ML potentials can accurately reproduce vibrational and anharmonic entropy contributions
Thermodynamic integration with an ML potential yields a ~10x speedup over full AIMD/TOR-TILD
The method maintains 5–10% accuracy in free energies and fusion properties for elemental/binary systems
